title: Celestin's 1920s recordings and second trumpet
summary: Which musicians played on the Celestin recordings such as My Josephine and who was second trumpet.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Who was playing on the sax? Well, I remember the first on the saxophone had Joe Rouget, Edmund Hall. Edmund Hall. Oh, yeah. And Clarence Hall. See? So Edmund Hall, he jumped down and they took Earl Peterson. He don't play anymore. He's on the road now. He's a- We met him on a train, yeah. Yeah. And then after that, well, that's the way it's switched up about. But our first band was with Papa Celestine. And we did that recording and all of that. My Josephine and all of that. That was Paul Bones. My Josephine and all of that. My Josephine and all of that. My Josephine and all of that. This boy is sing. I just remember his name. Aida Cheri. No, not Aida Cheri. That's Sidney- Correa or something? That's Sidney Correa, Simon Moreira, John Moreira, August Russo, I think. I was known as Josephine. August Russo, I think it was playing as Josephine. Who was the second trumpet?
Second trumpet at that time. Let me see. With Papa Celestine was the second trumpet. I know it wasn't Guy because Guy wasn't, Guy hadn't come to New Orleans yet. How was Sniety? Sniety. Sniety.
Have a Sniety. Did you ever make any records with Kid Schatz or Ricard Alexis? Ricard Alexis? Was he on any of those?
Oh, that was Papa Celestine. We recorded for A La Bar and Maryland and High Society. The real old ones. I mean the real old band though in the 1920s.
That's who Ricard was the one playing second trumpet with Papa Celestine and made that Josephine. That's what it was. Ricard, he was playing. Ricard made that Ricard. That's fine. That's good.
Did the Shots Madison ever play on the records with you in the old days? Ricard. Shots. You know, Shots. Kid Schatz Madison. All you talking about Shots? Shots. Oh, sure. Was he on the records?
